title: 2nd Sitting of second session of 2026

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/2/2/2026).
Approval of the minutes of six previous sittings (minutes Nos. 15/1/2026 to 20/1/2026).

From the Speaker's desk: the President's nominations of non-resident ambassadors to foreign countries, under Article 115(d) of the Constitution and Article 14 of the Foreign Service Act (Law No. 20/2021), are sent to the relevant standing committee for review.

From the Speaker's desk: the President, using his powers under Article 116(a) of the Constitution, has changed the names and mandates of some ministries and re-drawn their areas of work; the request for Parliament's approval of the new mandates is sent to the relevant standing committee.

From the Speaker's desk: the President's nomination of a member to the Elections Commission, under Article 4(b) of the Elections Commission Act (Law No. 8/2008), is sent to the relevant standing committee for review.

From the Speaker's desk: the President's appointment of Hassan Zareer as Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises under Article 129(a) of the Constitution, submitted for Parliament's consent under Article 129(d), is sent to the relevant standing committee for review.

Motion under Rule 201 of the Standing Orders by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim for a debate on retired police and military personnel losing their retirement benefit when they take another state job or a government-company job, and the financial and social harm this causes them.
First reading of the resolution by Galolhu South MP Meekail Ahmed Naseem noting that councillors' pay needs a positive change and seeking members' views on it.
First reading of the Maldives 2.0 Digital Transformation Bill, submitted on behalf of the government by Gadhdhoo MP Mohamed Ali.
First reading of the Digital Identity Bill, submitted on behalf of the government by Alifushi MP Abdul Latheef Abdul Rahman.
Unfinished business: debate continues on the Cyber Security Bill, submitted on behalf of the government by Medhu Henveiru MP Hussain Nasih.
Unfinished business: debate continues on the Personal Data Protection Bill, submitted on behalf of the government by Henveiru West MP Ali Ibrahim.
Report of the Foreign Relations Committee on the President's nominations of ambassadors to the United Arab Emirates and the State of Qatar.
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: A packed sitting sending ambassador, Elections Commission, ministry-restructure and Finance Minister appointments to committees, introducing the Maldives 2.0 and Digital Identity bills, debating a police and military pensions motion, and continuing the Cyber Security and Data Protection bills.
